alignment_tool_analysis.about_the_organisation: Parkway is a financial technology company operating in Nigeria's fintech sector, delivering a suite of products across consumer and institutional segments. The organisation's primary offering is a consumer wallet product that provides virtual card functionality, enabling users to manage subscriptions (including services such as Google and Canva), participate in cooperative savings arrangements, and conduct digital transactions. Beyond the consumer wallet, Parkway operates in hospital-linked payment collection through a sister company that secures government contracts at state level, though this institutional segment functions as a closed loop requiring minimal marketing intervention. The brand also maintains a cooperative-focused product line earmarked for future rollout. Parkway's leadership has identified the consumer wallet as the immediate growth driver requiring marketing support, reflecting a strategic choice to concentrate resources on the B2C segment before expanding to cooperatives. The organisation is positioning its wallet as an everyday financial utility with broad household penetration ambitions, distinguished by its virtual card capabilities in a market where digital payment infrastructure continues to mature. Parkway's current commercial context centres on user acquisition velocity in a competitive consumer fintech landscape, with the team demonstrating a disciplined approach to segment prioritisation rather than pursuing multiple verticals simultaneously.
alignment_tool_analysis.core_focus_areas: The immediate focus area is the consumer wallet product, which the organisation has designated as the first-phase marketing priority. The wallet's virtual card feature represents a core value proposition, supporting subscription payments and cooperative participation use cases. The leadership team has explicitly deprioritised hospital payment collection activities because these operate through a sister company managing government negotiations and state contracts, effectively functioning as a closed-loop business requiring no external marketing. Cooperatives have been identified as a second-phase opportunity once the consumer wallet achieves traction. The organisation is concentrating on broad consumer adoption of the wallet product, with the stated ambition to place the wallet in the hands of every potential user, signalling mass-market intent rather than niche positioning.
alignment_tool_analysis.key_customers_beneficiaries: The primary customer segment is B2C consumers who require digital wallet services for everyday financial transactions, subscription management, and participation in cooperative savings structures. The consumer base includes individuals using the wallet for recurring digital service payments such as streaming platforms, productivity tools, and other subscription-based services that accept virtual card payments. The wallet also serves consumers seeking to enhance their financial participation through cooperative membership, suggesting an audience interested in both transactional convenience and structured savings. The hospital payment collection segment, while part of Parkway's broader ecosystem, targets institutional clients through a separate sister company and does not represent a marketing-driven customer base. The phased approach to cooperatives indicates a secondary audience of group savings participants and cooperative administrators who will become priority customers once the initial consumer wallet rollout demonstrates market validation.
alignment_tool_analysis.key_goals_metrics: The organisation has set a quantified user acquisition target of 100,000 additional B2C wallet users per quarter, serving as the primary success metric for the consumer wallet initiative. This quarterly benchmark translates to a pro-rated expectation of 200,000 new users before year-end, acknowledging the engagement is beginning partway through the third quarter. The leadership team confirmed this growth target represents significant and desirable performance, using it as the planning baseline for campaign development. Success is measured through net new user additions rather than transaction volume, wallet balances, or revenue metrics in the available conversation, indicating that initial growth strategy prioritises user base expansion and market penetration velocity. The team referenced these targets as captured documentation reviewed during the engagement, with unanimous affirmation that achieving the stated volume would constitute meaningful commercial progress for the business.
alignment_tool_analysis.success_timeline: The organisation is operating on a phased rollout timeline beginning with the consumer wallet as the immediate priority, followed by cooperatives in a subsequent phase. The engagement conversation occurred during the third quarter of the calendar year, with pro-rated user acquisition targets applied from that point through year-end. A follow-up milestone was scheduled for mid-August to review campaign concepts and budget recommendations, establishing a rhythm of iterative planning and execution rather than a single campaign launch. The phased approach defers cooperative segment marketing until the wallet achieves traction, though no explicit timeline for phase two transition was stated. The team emphasised flexibility in working models that can be adjusted as campaigns progress, suggesting an adaptive timeline responsive to performance data rather than fixed long-range commitments.
alignment_tool_analysis.focus: Parkway's marketing focus centres entirely on driving consumer adoption of the wallet product through a concentrated B2C acquisition campaign. The organisation has made an explicit strategic decision to narrow from multiple potential segments to a single priority, resisting the temptation to market across hospital collections, cooperatives, and wallet offerings simultaneously. This discipline reflects leadership experience that younger companies often dilute impact by pursuing too many initiatives concurrently. The wallet's value proposition emphasises everyday utility through virtual card functionality, positioning the product as essential infrastructure for digital subscription management rather than a novelty financial tool. The marketing agenda is to establish the wallet as ubiquitous consumer technology, with cooperatives and other segments deliberately held in reserve until the primary offering demonstrates market validation and sustainable growth.
alignment_tool_analysis.priority: The overriding priority is executing a B2C consumer wallet acquisition campaign capable of delivering 100,000 net new users per quarter, supported by creative concepts and budget allocations to be developed in the immediate engagement phase. Campaign development takes precedence over segment expansion, with the organisation explicitly deferring cooperative marketing and requiring no hospital collection support due to the closed-loop structure of that business line. The team prioritised clarity and focus, welcoming the recommendation to concentrate resources rather than fragment efforts across multiple audiences. Budget recommendations and pitch ideas represent the next critical deliverable, with approval contingent on the creative direction hitting strategic targets. The leadership team values over-planning relative to under-resourcing, indicating a priority on ambitious rather than conservative campaign scoping during the planning phase.

alignment_snapshot_fields.about_the_organisation: Parkway is a financial technology company operating in Nigeria's fintech sector, delivering a suite of products across consumer and institutional segments. The organisation's primary offering is a consumer wallet product that provides virtual card functionality, enabling users to manage subscriptions (including services such as Google and Canva), participate in cooperative savings arrangements, and conduct digital transactions. Beyond the consumer wallet, Parkway operates in hospital-linked payment collection through a sister company that secures government contracts at state level, though this institutional segment functions as a closed loop requiring minimal marketing intervention. The brand also maintains a cooperative-focused product line earmarked for future rollout. Parkway's leadership has identified the consumer wallet as the immediate growth driver requiring marketing support, reflecting a strategic choice to concentrate resources on the B2C segment before expanding to cooperatives. The organisation is positioning its wallet as an everyday financial utility with broad household penetration ambitions, distinguished by its virtual card capabilities in a market where digital payment infrastructure continues to mature. Parkway's current commercial context centres on user acquisition velocity in a competitive consumer fintech landscape, with the team demonstrating a disciplined approach to segment prioritisation rather than pursuing multiple verticals simultaneously.
alignment_snapshot_fields.core_focus_areas: The immediate focus area is the consumer wallet product, which the organisation has designated as the first-phase marketing priority. The wallet's virtual card feature represents a core value proposition, supporting subscription payments and cooperative participation use cases. The leadership team has explicitly deprioritised hospital payment collection activities because these operate through a sister company managing government negotiations and state contracts, effectively functioning as a closed-loop business requiring no external marketing. Cooperatives have been identified as a second-phase opportunity once the consumer wallet achieves traction. The organisation is concentrating on broad consumer adoption of the wallet product, with the stated ambition to place the wallet in the hands of every potential user, signalling mass-market intent rather than niche positioning.
alignment_snapshot_fields.key_customers_beneficiaries: The primary customer segment is B2C consumers who require digital wallet services for everyday financial transactions, subscription management, and participation in cooperative savings structures. The consumer base includes individuals using the wallet for recurring digital service payments such as streaming platforms, productivity tools, and other subscription-based services that accept virtual card payments. The wallet also serves consumers seeking to enhance their financial participation through cooperative membership, suggesting an audience interested in both transactional convenience and structured savings. The hospital payment collection segment, while part of Parkway's broader ecosystem, targets institutional clients through a separate sister company and does not represent a marketing-driven customer base. The phased approach to cooperatives indicates a secondary audience of group savings participants and cooperative administrators who will become priority customers once the initial consumer wallet rollout demonstrates market validation.
alignment_snapshot_fields.key_goals_metrics: The organisation has set a quantified user acquisition target of 100,000 additional B2C wallet users per quarter, serving as the primary success metric for the consumer wallet initiative. This quarterly benchmark translates to a pro-rated expectation of 200,000 new users before year-end, acknowledging the engagement is beginning partway through the third quarter. The leadership team confirmed this growth target represents significant and desirable performance, using it as the planning baseline for campaign development. Success is measured through net new user additions rather than transaction volume, wallet balances, or revenue metrics in the available conversation, indicating that initial growth strategy prioritises user base expansion and market penetration velocity. The team referenced these targets as captured documentation reviewed during the engagement, with unanimous affirmation that achieving the stated volume would constitute meaningful commercial progress for the business.
alignment_snapshot_fields.success_timeline: The organisation is operating on a phased rollout timeline beginning with the consumer wallet as the immediate priority, followed by cooperatives in a subsequent phase. The engagement conversation occurred during the third quarter of the calendar year, with pro-rated user acquisition targets applied from that point through year-end. A follow-up milestone was scheduled for mid-August to review campaign concepts and budget recommendations, establishing a rhythm of iterative planning and execution rather than a single campaign launch. The phased approach defers cooperative segment marketing until the wallet achieves traction, though no explicit timeline for phase two transition was stated. The team emphasised flexibility in working models that can be adjusted as campaigns progress, suggesting an adaptive timeline responsive to performance data rather than fixed long-range commitments.
alignment_snapshot_fields.focus: Parkway's marketing focus centres entirely on driving consumer adoption of the wallet product through a concentrated B2C acquisition campaign. The organisation has made an explicit strategic decision to narrow from multiple potential segments to a single priority, resisting the temptation to market across hospital collections, cooperatives, and wallet offerings simultaneously. This discipline reflects leadership experience that younger companies often dilute impact by pursuing too many initiatives concurrently. The wallet's value proposition emphasises everyday utility through virtual card functionality, positioning the product as essential infrastructure for digital subscription management rather than a novelty financial tool. The marketing agenda is to establish the wallet as ubiquitous consumer technology, with cooperatives and other segments deliberately held in reserve until the primary offering demonstrates market validation and sustainable growth.
alignment_snapshot_fields.priority: The overriding priority is executing a B2C consumer wallet acquisition campaign capable of delivering 100,000 net new users per quarter, supported by creative concepts and budget allocations to be developed in the immediate engagement phase. Campaign development takes precedence over segment expansion, with the organisation explicitly deferring cooperative marketing and requiring no hospital collection support due to the closed-loop structure of that business line. The team prioritised clarity and focus, welcoming the recommendation to concentrate resources rather than fragment efforts across multiple audiences. Budget recommendations and pitch ideas represent the next critical deliverable, with approval contingent on the creative direction hitting strategic targets. The leadership team values over-planning relative to under-resourcing, indicating a priority on ambitious rather than conservative campaign scoping during the planning phase.

Summary:

The team decided to prioritize the B2C consumer wallet and set growth targets for initial rollout.

Key Discussion Points:

Introductions and attendance
The call began with salutations and attendance checks, during which participants noted network issues and late joins that affected audio/video availability. Jude, Chidi, Diana, Seyelnen, and others established presence and confirmed readiness to proceed.

Review of recap and recommended focus
The team reviewed the recap shared by Emma/Sianni and agreed the document reflected current activities, but urged narrowing to one primary segment to start. Chidi emphasized that some segments are closed loops and therefore not marketing priorities.

Determining primary target — wallet (B2C)
Discussion centered on selecting the consumer wallet as the first-phase priority because it needs marketing and has clear value propositions. Chidi described wallet features, use cases like virtual cards for subscriptions, and suggested cooperatives be a second-phase focus.

Growth target and success metrics
Jude raised questions about defining success and whether targets were captured; the team reviewed the plan and agreed on a simple metric of 100,000 additional B2C users per quarter as a planning baseline. Participants affirmed that this target aligns with desired growth.

Next steps, deliverables, and scheduling
The group agreed to prepare campaign and creative pitch ideas and, if approved, produce budget recommendations. Scheduling was discussed; Seyelnen recommended a later week and Jude proposed reconvening in mid-August, with Chidi confirming a meeting date and Jude to distribute the meeting link and pre-read materials.

Closing and informal wrap-up
Final remarks included light closing banter and confirmations to meet again, with participants expressing readiness to follow through on assigned preparations and to attend the scheduled follow-up.

--- Session 1 | 2026-09-07 ---
Summary:

The team decided to prioritize the B2C consumer wallet and set growth targets for initial rollout.
• Prioritize B2C consumer wallet launch
• Target 100,000 new users per quarter
• Defer cooperatives to phase two
• Jude committed campaign concepts and budgets
• Reconvene mid-August, meeting date 14 August

Action Items:

* Meeting participants will prepare campaign and creative pitch ideas for the wallet B2C segment
* Jude will send the meeting link for the follow-up session
* Meeting participants will send supporting information and materials ahead of the next presentation
* Chidi Dire will schedule the follow-up meeting on 14th of August

Key Discussion Points:

Introductions and attendance
The call began with salutations and attendance checks, during which participants noted network issues and late joins that affected audio/video availability. Jude, Chidi, Diana, Seyelnen, and others established presence and confirmed readiness to proceed.

Review of recap and recommended focus
The team reviewed the recap shared by Emma/Sianni and agreed the document reflected current activities, but urged narrowing to one primary segment to start. Chidi emphasized that some segments are closed loops and therefore not marketing priorities.

Determining primary target — wallet (B2C)
Discussion centered on selecting the consumer wallet as the first-phase priority because it needs marketing and has clear value propositions. Chidi described wallet features, use cases like virtual cards for subscriptions, and suggested cooperatives be a second-phase focus.

Growth target and success metrics
Jude raised questions about defining success and whether targets were captured; the team reviewed the plan and agreed on a simple metric of 100,000 additional B2C users per quarter as a planning baseline. Participants affirmed that this target aligns with desired growth.

Next steps, deliverables, and scheduling
The group agreed to prepare campaign and creative pitch ideas and, if approved, produce budget recommendations. Scheduling was discussed; Seyelnen recommended a later week and Jude proposed reconvening in mid-August, with Chidi confirming a meeting date and Jude to distribute the meeting link and pre-read materials.

Closing and informal wrap-up
Final remarks included light closing banter and confirmations to meet again, with participants expressing readiness to follow through on assigned preparations and to attend the scheduled follow-up.

TASCK would like to talk through your brand and what you are working to achieve, so we can shape the right approach with you. We would like to cover:

1. Your brand / organisation - who you are, what you do, and who you serve.
2. Core Focus Areas - the priorities that matter most to you right now.

5. Audience Behaviour / Pain Points - what they do today, and what gets in their way.

7. What Success Looks Like / Timeline - your definition of a win, and by when.

sections.heading: PLUTO VERIFYME.NG - TRUST BEGINS AT HOME
sections.content:
PLUTO VERIFYME.NG - TRUST BEGINS AT HOME
AT HOME
Celebrity-Led Consumer Education Campaign
Moving household security from reactive to proactive through trusted verification

sections.heading: About The Organisation
sections.content:
Pluto (Verifyme.NG)
Pluto operates under Verifyme.NG as a Nigerian technology company specializing in digital identity verification and authentication solutions. The platform serves the Nigerian market with verification technology focused on KYC compliance, identity management, and background screening.
Historically positioned as a B2B background-check service, Pluto now aims to bring its verification infrastructure directly to Nigerian households, enabling families to make informed hiring decisions for domestic workers and artisans.
Digital Identity Verification
Nigerian Market Focus
Established verification technology platform serving Nigerian businesses
Proprietary database infrastructure for employee performance tracking
Unique Pluto Radar feature enabling shared reporting across users
Ready infrastructure for consumer-facing product expansion
Opportunity in Nigeria
Nigerian households consistently hire domestic workers, drivers, nannies, and artisans without adequate background information, creating significant security and trust gaps.
The market opportunity lies in democratizing B2B verification tools for mass consumer use, transforming household hiring from a risk-based gamble into an informed, secure decision.

sections.heading: Context & Core Focus
sections.content:
From Enterprise Background Checks
to Household Peace of Mind
Current Reality - Pluto exists as a B2B verification service known primarily within corporate and HR circles. Consumers hire household staff based on referrals, intuition, or informal networks with no access to verified employment history or performance data.
Strategic Opportunity - Nigerian households represent an untapped mass market desperate for security solutions. By repositioning the same verification technology as a consumer protection tool, Pluto can own the household hiring category while building long-term platform adoption.
Campaign Goal - Shift Pluto from B2B infrastructure to a trusted household name. Use celebrity storytelling and the original VerifyMe origin story to drive awareness, consideration, and conversion among urban millennials and extended demographics up to age 65.

sections.heading: The Problem
sections.content:
Nigerians Hire Blind, Then Hope for the Best
Household hiring happens in an information vacuum, leaving families vulnerable to theft, harm, and broken trust.
Domestic workers and artisans are hired based on word-of-mouth with no verified employment history
Security incidents are reactive - families only verify after something goes wrong
Older demographics rely on children to navigate unfamiliar tech platforms, creating adoption friction
No shared database exists for reporting worker performance or flagging issues across households
Verification is perceived as complex, inconvenient, or only necessary after an incident occurs
The gap is not awareness of risk. The gap is accessible, simple tools that make verification feel urgent before harm happens.

sections.heading: The Objective
sections.content:
Make Household Verification a Non-Negotiable Behaviour
Drive mass adoption of Pluto as the default step before any household hiring decision.
Business Objectives
Transition Pluto from B2B service to mass-market consumer brand
Achieve 120,000 registered consumer users within 12 months
Establish Pluto Radar as the trusted shared database for household hiring
Build sustainable user acquisition through referral loops and platform stickiness
Behaviour Objectives
Normalize verification as a proactive habit, not a post-incident reaction
Shift hiring decisions from trust-based referrals to data-informed choices
Empower older demographics to engage with verification through simplified onboarding
Create peer accountability through shared reporting and transparent worker histories

sections.heading: The Market / Core Audience
sections.content:
Urban Millennials with Household Hiring Responsibility (25-65)
Middle-income Nigerian families hiring domestic workers, drivers, nannies, cooks, and artisans for their homes.
Audience Persona
Adaeze Okonkwo - 38
Lives in Lagos, married with two children under 10
Employs a full-time nanny and cleaner, occasionally hires plumbers and electricians
Relies on referrals from friends but has experienced theft and unreliable workers in the past
Tech-comfortable but values simplicity and speed over feature complexity
Willing to pay for peace of mind and proactive security
Trusts celebrity endorsements from figures she respects
Shares household management decisions with extended family members aged 50-65
Market Size
Estimated 4 million Nigerian households actively hiring domestic workers or artisans, concentrated in Lagos, Abuja, and Port Harcourt
Initial Focus
Lagos urban and suburban middle-income families
Abuja professional households
Extended family decision-makers aged 50-65

sections.heading: The Solution / Creator Strategy
sections.content:
Trust the Story, Then Trust the Platform
Celebrity ambassador Adesua Etomi Wellington will anchor the campaign by telling the original VerifyMe origin story - a narrative rooted in real pain, real risk, and a homegrown Nigerian solution. Her credibility, household relatability, and cross-generational appeal make her the bridge between brand and behaviour change.
Supporting creators will demonstrate the platform through real-life use cases, customer testimonials, and product walkthroughs. The campaign moves audiences from emotional connection to practical adoption, using storytelling to create urgency and creator content to remove friction.
Suggested Creator Profiles
Celebrity Ambassador - Trusted household figure with cross-generational reach
Lifestyle Creators - Family-focused influencers sharing hiring experiences
Tech Explainers - Simplifying platform features for non-tech audiences
Customer Advocates - Real Pluto users sharing testimonials and results
Their Roles
Tell the VerifyMe origin story to build emotional connection and brand trust
Demonstrate the Pluto platform with step-by-step walkthroughs and ease-of-use proof
Share real customer stories of incidents avoided and peace of mind gained
Normalize verification as a standard household behaviour through repeated messaging
Drive referral loops by encouraging users to share their own verification experiences
Address older demographics through simplified, reassuring content formats

sections.heading: Go-To-Market / Campaign
sections.content:
Three-Stage Consumer Adoption Journey
(Months 1-3) - Awareness - The Story - Introduce VerifyMe as the trusted solution for household security by educating Nigerians on the risks of hiring without verification. - Activities - Reach 2.4 million Nigerians with the message that hiring without verification is a gamble they no longer need to take.
Adesua Etomi Wellington launches campaign with VerifyMe origin story across Instagram, Facebook, TikTok
Emotional storytelling content highlighting real household incidents and preventable harm
Paid media amplification targeting urban millennials and household decision-makers
PR seeding around household security trends and verification technology
(Months 4-7) - Consideration - The Product - Use creator stories, customer testimonials, and product demonstrations to encourage platform exploration and understanding. - Activities - Move 600,000 Nigerians from awareness to active platform consideration and account exploration.
Lifestyle creators share real-life use cases of verifying nannies, drivers, and artisans
Tech explainer content walking through Pluto onboarding, Radar feature, and reporting tools
Customer testimonial videos from early adopters sharing peace of mind and positive experiences
Retargeting campaigns to awareness audience with product education and ease-of-use proof
(Months 8-12) - Conversion - The Habit - Convert interested audiences into registered users through targeted campaigns, limited offers, and referral incentives. - Activities - Achieve 120,000 registered users actively using Pluto to verify household hires and contribute to the shared database.
Strong call-to-action campaigns with limited-time onboarding offers and first-verification discounts
Referral program activation encouraging users to invite friends and family
Adesua-led conversion push emphasizing the one-time cost of peace of mind versus lifetime risk
Platform optimization based on user feedback to reduce friction for older demographics
(Ongoing) - Retention - The Community - Build platform stickiness through shared reporting, repeat verification use, and community-driven accountability. - Activities - Create a self-sustaining verification culture where users return to the platform for every new hire and contribute to collective security.
Encourage users to log worker performance and flag issues on Pluto Radar
Seasonal campaigns around holiday hiring peaks and new worker onboarding moments
User-generated content showcasing real stories of verification preventing incidents
Ambassador partnerships with household management influencers for sustained visibility

sections.heading: Go-To-Market / Campaign
sections.content:
The Consumer Adoption Funnel
Awareness - 4,000,000 reach - Urban Nigerians exposed to VerifyMe story and household security messaging
Engagement - 2,400,000 engaged - Audiences watching product demos, testimonials, and creator walkthroughs
Consideration - 600,000 considering - Platform visitors exploring features, pricing, and onboarding process
Conversion - 120,000 registered users - Active accounts verifying household hires and using Pluto Radar
Advocacy - Referral-driven growth - Users inviting friends, sharing experiences, contributing to database
Primary Platforms
Instagram
Facebook
TikTok
Secondary Platforms
YouTube for long-form origin story
WhatsApp for peer sharing and referral loops
Twitter for PR amplification and thought leadership
Google Search for intent-driven discovery

sections.heading: Campaign Projections
sections.content:
Success Metrics (12 Months)
Community Growth
120,000 registered consumer users
4,000,000 total reach across platforms
600,000 engaged consideration audience
Content
60+ pieces of creator and ambassador content
2.4 million video views on awareness storytelling
8,000+ user-generated testimonials and shared experiences
Commercial
120,000 paying users completing first verification
Average 2.3 verifications per user annually
40% referral-driven acquisition by Month 12
Behaviour
Verification becomes standard practice before household hiring
Pluto Radar database grows with shared worker performance reports
Platform stickiness drives repeat use for every new hiring decision
Older demographics successfully onboard with family support and simplified UX

sections.heading: Risk & Mitigation Analysis
sections.content:
Risk & Mitigation Analysis
Platform perceived as too complex or inconvenient for quick household hiring decisions - Showcase simple, fast user journey through product demos, creator walkthroughs, and clear messaging around speed and ease of use. Optimize onboarding flow based on early user feedback.
Low urgency - consumers only seek verification after an incident occurs rather than proactively - Preventive messaging emphasizes peace of mind and proactive protection. Emotional storytelling from Adesua and real testimonials create urgency before harm happens.
Difficulty converting awareness into paid users due to cost sensitivity or perceived value gap - Use testimonials, limited-time offers, and strong calls-to-action to move users from interest to adoption. Highlight the one-time cost versus lifetime risk positioning.
Older demographics struggle with tech adoption and rely on children to navigate platform - Create simplified onboarding content specifically for non-tech audiences. Use Adesua to model intergenerational use and reassure older users. Offer phone support during pilot phase.
Database growth depends on user contributions - slow Radar adoption limits platform value - Incentivize reporting through referral rewards and community recognition. Make reporting simple and emphasize collective security benefits.
Celebrity ambassador association limits brand independence or creates over-reliance on single voice - Build supporting creator ecosystem early. Transition Adesua from lead storyteller to brand advocate while elevating customer stories and user-generated content.

sections.heading: Budget Assumptions
sections.content:
12-Month Pilot Investment
Estimated Budget
$150,000 - $200,000 USD
Budget Includes
Celebrity ambassador partnership - Adesua Etomi Wellington (storytelling, campaign launch, sustained visibility)
Supporting creator partnerships - lifestyle, tech explainer, and customer advocate content
Paid media - Meta, TikTok, Google, YouTube amplification across awareness, consideration, conversion stages
Content production - origin story video, product demos, testimonials, user walkthroughs
Platform optimization - UX improvements for older demographics and onboarding friction reduction
Referral program activation - incentive structure, tracking, and promotion
Campaign management - strategy, creator coordination, performance tracking, reporting
Contingency - 10% for platform adjustments and market response flexibility
A successful pilot unlocks national expansion, additional creator tiers, and sustained investment in platform-driven community growth.

sections.heading: Talent Suggestions / Team
sections.content:
Recommended Creator Mix
Adesua Etomi Wellington - 8M+ across Instagram, Facebook, Twitter - Trusted household name with cross-generational appeal, credibility in family and lifestyle spaces, and storytelling strength to anchor the VerifyMe origin narrative - Celebrity Ambassador - Campaign anchor, origin story lead, sustained brand voice across all stages
Supporting Lifestyle Creators (TBD based on audience alignment) - 500K-2M per creator - Family-focused influencers who share relatable household hiring experiences and model proactive verification behaviour - Awareness & Consideration - Real-life use cases, product demonstrations, testimonial amplification
Tech Explainer Creators (TBD based on platform simplicity focus) - 200K-1M per creator - Ability to break down Pluto features for non-tech audiences, especially older demographics requiring reassurance and guidance - Consideration - Platform walkthroughs, onboarding tutorials, ease-of-use proof
Customer Advocates (Real Pluto Users) - Organic reach through user-generated content - Authentic testimonials from actual users sharing peace of mind, incidents avoided, and positive verification experiences - Conversion & Retention - Social proof, referral encouragement, community building
Why This Mix Works
Adesua Etomi Wellington provides the emotional anchor and trust layer required to move a mass audience from skepticism to belief. Her household credibility makes verification feel urgent, accessible, and culturally relevant.
Supporting lifestyle creators demonstrate practical adoption and normalize verification as everyday behaviour. They move audiences from belief to consideration by showing real families using the platform in real hiring scenarios.
Tech explainers reduce friction for non-tech users and older demographics, addressing the convenience barrier head-on. Their content transforms platform complexity into simplicity, removing adoption resistance.
Customer advocates provide the social proof that drives conversion. Real users sharing real results create the peer pressure and community accountability that turn individual adoption into collective behaviour change.
Supporting creator selections will be finalized during onboarding to ensure audience alignment, platform strength, and content quality standards.

sections.heading: Delivery Team
sections.content:
Delivery Team
Strategy & Campaign Management
Campaign strategy, positioning, and messaging framework
Creator identification, negotiation, and partnership management
Content planning, editorial calendars, and creative direction
Performance tracking, reporting, and optimization recommendations
Content Production & Amplification
Video production for origin story, product demos, and testimonials
Creator content coordination and quality assurance
Paid media planning, execution, and budget management across Meta, TikTok, Google
Platform optimization support and UX feedback loops
Client Partnership & Platform Integration
Pluto internal stakeholder alignment and briefing
Platform feature prioritization based on campaign learnings
Referral program design and tracking integration
Customer support coordination for pilot phase user inquiries

sections.heading: Closing Statement
sections.content:
Trust Cannot Be Purchased After the Incident
Nigerian households are hiring blind every single day. Pluto has the infrastructure, the technology, and the database to change that behaviour - but infrastructure does not move markets. Stories do. Trust does. Urgency does.
This campaign transforms Pluto from a B2B service into a household necessity by making verification feel urgent before harm happens, simple enough for anyone to use, and socially reinforced through shared accountability. A successful pilot does not just deliver 120,000 users. It creates a verification culture that becomes the new standard for how Nigerians hire, protect their families, and build collective security. That culture is worth far more than the campaign investment.

items: Transition Pluto from B2B service to mass-market consumer brand
Achieve 120,000 registered consumer users within 12 months
Establish Pluto Radar as the trusted shared database for household hiring
Build sustainable user acquisition through referral loops and platform stickiness

columns.label: Behaviour Objectives
items: Normalize verification as a proactive habit, not a post-incident reaction
Shift hiring decisions from trust-based referrals to data-informed choices
Empower older demographics to engage with verification through simplified onboarding
Create peer accountability through shared reporting and transparent worker histories

market.title: Urban Millennials with Household Hiring Responsibility (25-65)
market.lead: Middle-income Nigerian families hiring domestic workers, drivers, nannies, cooks, and artisans for their homes.
traits: Lives in Lagos, married with two children under 10
Employs a full-time nanny and cleaner, occasionally hires plumbers and electricians
Relies on referrals from friends but has experienced theft and unreliable workers in the past
Tech-comfortable but values simplicity and speed over feature complexity
Willing to pay for peace of mind and proactive security
Trusts celebrity endorsements from figures she respects
Shares household management decisions with extended family members aged 50-65
market.market_size: Estimated 4 million Nigerian households actively hiring domestic workers or artisans, concentrated in Lagos, Abuja, and Port Harcourt
initial_focus: Lagos urban and suburban middle-income families

solution.title: Trust the Story, Then Trust the Platform
paragraphs: Celebrity ambassador Adesua Etomi Wellington will anchor the campaign by telling the original VerifyMe origin story - a narrative rooted in real pain, real risk, and a homegrown Nigerian solution. Her credibility, household relatability, and cross-generational appeal make her the bridge between brand and behaviour change.

Supporting creators will demonstrate the platform through real-life use cases, customer testimonials, and product walkthroughs. The campaign moves audiences from emotional connection to practical adoption, using storytelling to create urgency and creator content to remove friction.
suggested: Celebrity Ambassador - Trusted household figure with cross-generational reach
Lifestyle Creators - Family-focused influencers sharing hiring experiences
Tech Explainers - Simplifying platform features for non-tech audiences
Customer Advocates - Real Pluto users sharing testimonials and results
roles: Tell the VerifyMe origin story to build emotional connection and brand trust
Demonstrate the Pluto platform with step-by-step walkthroughs and ease-of-use proof
Share real customer stories of incidents avoided and peace of mind gained
Normalize verification as a standard household behaviour through repeated messaging
Drive referral loops by encouraging users to share their own verification experiences
Address older demographics through simplified, reassuring content formats

stages.title: Awareness - The Story
stages.lead: Introduce VerifyMe as the trusted solution for household security by educating Nigerians on the risks of hiring without verification.
activities: Adesua Etomi Wellington launches campaign with VerifyMe origin story across Instagram, Facebook, TikTok
Emotional storytelling content highlighting real household incidents and preventable harm
Paid media amplification targeting urban millennials and household decision-makers
PR seeding around household security trends and verification technology
stages.goal: Reach 2.4 million Nigerians with the message that hiring without verification is a gamble they no longer need to take.

stages.title: Consideration - The Product
stages.lead: Use creator stories, customer testimonials, and product demonstrations to encourage platform exploration and understanding.
activities: Lifestyle creators share real-life use cases of verifying nannies, drivers, and artisans
Tech explainer content walking through Pluto onboarding, Radar feature, and reporting tools
Customer testimonial videos from early adopters sharing peace of mind and positive experiences
Retargeting campaigns to awareness audience with product education and ease-of-use proof
stages.goal: Move 600,000 Nigerians from awareness to active platform consideration and account exploration.

stages.title: Conversion - The Habit
stages.lead: Convert interested audiences into registered users through targeted campaigns, limited offers, and referral incentives.
activities: Strong call-to-action campaigns with limited-time onboarding offers and first-verification discounts
Referral program activation encouraging users to invite friends and family
Adesua-led conversion push emphasizing the one-time cost of peace of mind versus lifetime risk
Platform optimization based on user feedback to reduce friction for older demographics
stages.goal: Achieve 120,000 registered users actively using Pluto to verify household hires and contribute to the shared database.

stages.title: Retention - The Community
stages.lead: Build platform stickiness through shared reporting, repeat verification use, and community-driven accountability.
activities: Encourage users to log worker performance and flag issues on Pluto Radar
Seasonal campaigns around holiday hiring peaks and new worker onboarding moments
User-generated content showcasing real stories of verification preventing incidents
Ambassador partnerships with household management influencers for sustained visibility
stages.goal: Create a self-sustaining verification culture where users return to the platform for every new hire and contribute to collective security.

rows.risk: Platform perceived as too complex or inconvenient for quick household hiring decisions
rows.mitigation: Showcase simple, fast user journey through product demos, creator walkthroughs, and clear messaging around speed and ease of use. Optimize onboarding flow based on early user feedback.

rows.risk: Low urgency - consumers only seek verification after an incident occurs rather than proactively
rows.mitigation: Preventive messaging emphasizes peace of mind and proactive protection. Emotional storytelling from Adesua and real testimonials create urgency before harm happens.

rows.risk: Difficulty converting awareness into paid users due to cost sensitivity or perceived value gap
rows.mitigation: Use testimonials, limited-time offers, and strong calls-to-action to move users from interest to adoption. Highlight the one-time cost versus lifetime risk positioning.

rows.risk: Older demographics struggle with tech adoption and rely on children to navigate platform
rows.mitigation: Create simplified onboarding content specifically for non-tech audiences. Use Adesua to model intergenerational use and reassure older users. Offer phone support during pilot phase.

rows.risk: Database growth depends on user contributions - slow Radar adoption limits platform value
rows.mitigation: Incentivize reporting through referral rewards and community recognition. Make reporting simple and emphasize collective security benefits.

rows.risk: Celebrity ambassador association limits brand independence or creates over-reliance on single voice
rows.mitigation: Build supporting creator ecosystem early. Transition Adesua from lead storyteller to brand advocate while elevating customer stories and user-generated content.

includes: Celebrity ambassador partnership - Adesua Etomi Wellington (storytelling, campaign launch, sustained visibility)
Supporting creator partnerships - lifestyle, tech explainer, and customer advocate content
Paid media - Meta, TikTok, Google, YouTube amplification across awareness, consideration, conversion stages
Content production - origin story video, product demos, testimonials, user walkthroughs
Platform optimization - UX improvements for older demographics and onboarding friction reduction
Referral program activation - incentive structure, tracking, and promotion
Campaign management - strategy, creator coordination, performance tracking, reporting
Contingency - 10% for platform adjustments and market response flexibility
budget.footnote: A successful pilot unlocks national expansion, additional creator tiers, and sustained investment in platform-driven community growth.

rows.role: Celebrity Ambassador - Campaign anchor, origin story lead, sustained brand voice across all stages

rows.role: Awareness & Consideration - Real-life use cases, product demonstrations, testimonial amplification

rows.why: Ability to break down Pluto features for non-tech audiences, especially older demographics requiring reassurance and guidance

rows.why: Authentic testimonials from actual users sharing peace of mind, incidents avoided, and positive verification experiences
rows.role: Conversion & Retention - Social proof, referral encouragement, community building

why_works: Adesua Etomi Wellington provides the emotional anchor and trust layer required to move a mass audience from skepticism to belief. Her household credibility makes verification feel urgent, accessible, and culturally relevant.

Supporting lifestyle creators demonstrate practical adoption and normalize verification as everyday behaviour. They move audiences from belief to consideration by showing real families using the platform in real hiring scenarios.

Tech explainers reduce friction for non-tech users and older demographics, addressing the convenience barrier head-on. Their content transforms platform complexity into simplicity, removing adoption resistance.

Customer advocates provide the social proof that drives conversion. Real users sharing real results create the peer pressure and community accountability that turn individual adoption into collective behaviour change.
creator_mix.footnote: Supporting creator selections will be finalized during onboarding to ensure audience alignment, platform strength, and content quality standards.

cards.title: Strategy & Campaign Management
items: Campaign strategy, positioning, and messaging framework
Creator identification, negotiation, and partnership management
Content planning, editorial calendars, and creative direction
Performance tracking, reporting, and optimization recommendations

cards.title: Content Production & Amplification
items: Video production for origin story, product demos, and testimonials
Creator content coordination and quality assurance
Paid media planning, execution, and budget management across Meta, TikTok, Google
Platform optimization support and UX feedback loops

cards.title: Client Partnership & Platform Integration
items: Pluto internal stakeholder alignment and briefing
Platform feature prioritization based on campaign learnings
Referral program design and tracking integration
Customer support coordination for pilot phase user inquiries

closing.title: Trust Cannot Be Purchased After the Incident
paragraphs: Nigerian households are hiring blind every single day. Pluto has the infrastructure, the technology, and the database to change that behaviour - but infrastructure does not move markets. Stories do. Trust does. Urgency does.

This campaign transforms Pluto from a B2B service into a household necessity by making verification feel urgent before harm happens, simple enough for anyone to use, and socially reinforced through shared accountability. A successful pilot does not just deliver 120,000 users. It creates a verification culture that becomes the new standard for how Nigerians hire, protect their families, and build collective security. That culture is worth far more than the campaign investment.

contract.title: PLUTO Verifyme.NG x TASCK - Service Agreement

sections.heading: Service Agreement
sections.content: This Service Agreement is dated 2026-09-03 and is made between TASCK Creative Company Limited, trading as The TASCK Agency ('TASCK'), and PLUTO Verifyme.NG ('Brand') for the project titled PLUTO Verifyme.NG - Business Call Connect. It is written to be reviewed easily before approval and signature. It explains the project scope, responsibilities, commercial terms, approval process, delivery expectations, cancellation rules, and close-out requirements.

sections.heading: 1. Parties
sections.content:
Party 1: TASCK Creative Company Limited, a registered company situated in Lagos, Nigeria.
Party 2: PLUTO Verifyme.NG.

TASCK and the Brand may be referred to individually as a Party and collectively as the Parties. The Parties agree to work together professionally, respond to project communications within reasonable timelines, and keep all approval decisions clear and documented.

sections.heading: 2. Background and Purpose
sections.content: The Brand has engaged TASCK to support the planning and delivery of PLUTO Verifyme.NG - Business Call Connect. TASCK has the strategy, creator coordination, project management, production support, and reporting capability required to deliver the approved work. The purpose of this Agreement is to record the commercial and operational terms under which TASCK will provide those services.

sections.heading: 3. Scope of Services
sections.content: TASCK will provide services that may include strategy development, creator recommendation and coordination, creative briefing, project planning, production support, content or activation oversight, performance tracking, stakeholder communication, reporting, and project close-out. The exact deliverables, dates, channels, and approval steps will follow the approved Strategy Snapshot, creator brief, deliverables schedule, and any later written amendments approved by both Parties.

sections.heading: 4. Brand Responsibilities
sections.content: The Brand will provide accurate business information, timely approvals, access to required assets, brand guidelines, payment information, stakeholder availability, and feedback needed for TASCK to deliver the project. Delays in approval, funding, asset delivery, or stakeholder response may affect timelines and may require a revised delivery schedule.

sections.heading: 5. Commercial Terms and Payment
sections.content: The total fixed fee or approved working budget for this project is ₦250,000. Payment will follow the approved budget and payment schedule. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, the first payment tranche is required before work begins, and any balance is due according to the agreed milestone or final delivery schedule. Work outside the approved scope, including additional creators, extra production days, usage extensions, paid media rights, venue costs, third-party services, rush delivery, or revised deliverables, must be approved in writing before TASCK proceeds.

sections.heading: 6. Project Timeline and Approvals
sections.content: The project timeline will be confirmed through the approved Strategy Snapshot, deliverables schedule, and execution plan. TASCK will submit key materials for review where approval is required. The Brand should provide consolidated feedback so the project can move efficiently. Any change in approval route, decision maker, launch date, budget, or legal requirement must be communicated to TASCK as soon as it is known.

sections.heading: 7. Performance, Reporting, and Acceptance
sections.content: TASCK will coordinate delivery and provide a final report using the information available from the approved deliverables, creator outputs, campaign performance, and project records. The Brand will review the final report and provide feedback or acceptance within a reasonable period. Once accepted, the project may be closed in TASCK.

sections.heading: 8. Intellectual Property and Usage
sections.content: Ownership and usage rights for project materials will follow the approved brief, creator contracts, paid usage terms, and any written rights schedule. TASCK does not grant rights beyond those actually secured from creators, production partners, or third parties. The Brand must not extend usage, paid media, territory, duration, exclusivity, or adaptation beyond the approved rights without written confirmation.

sections.heading: 9. Confidentiality
sections.content: Each Party will keep confidential information private, including campaign plans, commercial terms, project documents, unpublished creative, contact information, account access, strategy materials, creator negotiations, and performance data. Confidential information may only be shared with people who need it to perform the project.

sections.heading: 10. Cancellation, Delay, and Scope Changes
sections.content: If the Brand cancels, pauses, or materially changes the project after work has begun, TASCK will document the effect on schedule, cost, deliverables, third-party commitments, and creator obligations. The Brand remains responsible for approved work already completed, committed costs, cancellation charges, and reasonable time already spent. TASCK will not proceed with new or expanded work until the Parties approve the change in writing.

sections.heading: 11. Liability and Professional Conduct
sections.content: Each Party is responsible for its own negligence, misconduct, breach of confidentiality, and failure to meet documented obligations. Neither Party is responsible for delay or failure caused by events beyond reasonable control, including platform outages, government restrictions, force majeure events, third-party failure, or delayed approvals outside that Party's control.

sections.heading: 12. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution
sections.content: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. The Parties will first attempt to resolve any dispute through good-faith discussion. If unresolved, the dispute may be referred to arbitration in accordance with applicable Nigerian arbitration law.

Communication Strategy (Ambassador Approach) - July 15

VIEW RECORDING - 29 mins (No highlights)
Meeting Purpose
To explore a B2C communication strategy for the Pluto platform.
Key Takeaways
Goal: Shift Pluto from a B2B service to a mass-market B2C product, targeting 100k–200k users and ₦1.2B revenue in 12 months.
Product: Pluto is a background check platform with a unique "Pluto Radar" feature, a shared database for reporting employee performance (good or bad) to prevent re-hiring of flagged individuals.
Strategy: Use a celebrity ambassador to drive B2C adoption. The compensation model will blend a retainer with a performance-based component to align incentives.
Next Steps: Jude's team will deliver an "Alignment Snapshot" (business goals) by next week, followed by a campaign pitch with creator options ~7 days later.
Topics
The Challenge: Shifting from B2B to B2C
Pluto, a product of VerifyMe, is a background check platform with a B2B focus (KYC for fintech).
Goal: Pivot to a mass-market B2C product for household security.
Target Audience: Urban millennials (ages 30–40) in estates.
Business Potential:
Revenue: ₦1.2B in 12 months (from ₦1B target).
Users: 100k–200k.
Long-Term: 1M users → ₦10B revenue; 3M users → ₦30B revenue.
The Solution: Pluto Platform & Pluto Radar
Pluto offers comprehensive background checks for domestic staff, tenants, and business partners.
Core Features:
Identity & facial biometrics
Address verification via a 5,000–40,000 agent network
Guarantor & previous employment checks
Medical checks (EELTS)
Key Differentiator: Pluto Radar
A shared database for reporting employee performance (good or bad).
Mechanism: Employers submit detailed reports with evidence. The reported individual is notified (SMS/email) and can submit a dispute.
Outcome: A "red flag" is attached to the individual's profile, visible to future employers.
Rationale: Prevents individuals from changing names or locations to hide a history of theft, violence, or other serious incidents.
The Strategy: Celebrity Ambassador Campaign
Rationale: A celebrity ambassador can drive mass adoption and build public trust.
Compensation Model: A hybrid structure to align incentives.
Retainer: Standard payment for campaign assets.
Performance-Based: A percentage of revenue or user acquisition to reward success.
Campaign Approach: A structured, multi-phase campaign ("arc") is required, not just a single post.
Next Steps
Jude's Team:
Deliver an "Alignment Snapshot" (business goals) by next week.
Deliver a campaign pitch with creator options ~7 days after snapshot approval.
Esigie:
Review and approve the Alignment Snapshot to finalize campaign goals.

Jul 24, 2026
PLUTO Verifyme x TTA: Follow-Up Call
Invited e.aguele@verifyme.ng Jude | CEO m.maibe@verifyme.ng Seyelnen | Legal & Portfolio Lead Fanii | Head Of Music & Label. a.uti@verifyme.ng c.okonkwo@verifyme.ng n.kalango@verifyme.ng
Attachments PLUTO Verifyme x TTA: Follow-Up Call


Summary
Team refined strategic alignment documentation and verified audience demographics through identifying the national database differentiator.

Strategic Alignment Overview
Discussion focused on the business goals and audience demographics for domestic hiring security. The target range expanded to include individuals up to 65 years old.

Unique Value Proposition
Pluto Radar was introduced as a central database for reporting misconduct and verifying performance data. This establishes a competitive differentiator for the hiring platform.

Campaign Narrative Decision
Use of the original company origin story emerged as the preferred strategy for driving campaign engagement. This narrative emphasizes the necessity of a national security database.


Decisions
Aligned
Target audience age range expanded The target audience demographic is expanded to include individuals up to age 65 to better reflect the actual hiring behavior in the market.
Marketing strategy centered on Pluto radar The marketing campaign strategy is prioritized to highlight the unique 'Pluto radar' reporting and recommendation database as the primary product differentiator.

We've updated the Decisions section using your feedback.
Let us know what you think: Helpful or Not Helpful


Next steps
[Seyelnen] Grant Document Access: Provide editing access to the alignment document for all team members via email.
[The group] Edit Alignment Document: Review the alignment document and provide detailed feedback and corrections directly in the draft.
[The group] Schedule Meeting: Coordinate and confirm the next follow up meeting for the following week to proceed with campaign planning.
[Jude] Prepare Campaign Pitch: Develop campaign ideas and creator selections based on the project alignment to present at the next meeting.


Details
Team Introductions: Esigie Aguele introduced their team members, including Mohammed Maibe, the Senior Director for Operations, and Noya Kalango, the Director for Sales and Marketing. Seyelnen, representing the Legal & Portfolio Lead at Task, and Jude, the CEO and Founder of Task, also provided introductions to complete the team alignment.
Alignment Snapshot Overview: Seyelnen presented an "alignment snapshot" document intended to capture the business goals and target audiences. The document outlines a market opportunity in Nigeria regarding the hiring of domestic workers and artisans, where a lack of background information creates security risks for employers. The proposed solution is a product that provides background checks and mitigation measures to facilitate safe hiring.
Target Audience and Demographic Adjustments: The draft identified the primary audience as working adults aged 30 to 40 in urban areas, illustrated by an influencer persona. Esigie Aguele suggested expanding the target demographic to include individuals up to age 65, noting that older generations are frequent employers of domestic staff like drivers and often rely on their children to navigate tech platforms.
Business Goals and Revenue Metrics: The alignment document cited a goal of 1.2 billion in annual revenue and 100,000 to 200,000 users for household hires. Esigie Aguele invited the team to review these figures, noting the need to confirm they align with future projections. Jude emphasized that the document is a working draft intended to be critiqued and refined by the team.
Corporate Audience and Engagement: Seyelnen outlined a secondary audience segment consisting of employers and HR professionals looking to hire corporate talent. The success metrics for this segment include a 100% increase in monthly verification searches and a 100% increase in incident reports. Mohammed Maibe requested that the document include a specific profile of a business entity to better represent this audience segment, as the current draft focused on individual hires.
Campaign Strategy and Celebrity Archetypes: Jude explained that the next step involves reverse-engineering a campaign based on the validated target audience and goals. Esigie Aguele expressed interest in using celebrity personalities to drive retail sales. Seyelnen clarified that the selected celebrity archetype should be able to speak to both businesses and individuals. Jude noted that the team would later pitch four to five creators for the group to evaluate based on reach and audience influence.
Unique Value Proposition - Pluto Radar: Noya Kalango identified that the draft lacked a clear differentiator from other background check services. They introduced "Pluto Radar," a database for reporting and recommendations. This feature allows users to report misconduct or positive performance, provided there is evidence, and allows the accused party to refute claims. The consensus is to frame this as a "social good" and a national database, encouraging users to register their staff as part of a collective effort to improve safety.
Content and Celebrity Endorsement Strategy: Mohammed Maibe suggested utilizing a recognizable person who has experienced public hardship with domestic staff to promote the reporting angle. Esigie Aguele proposed using the origin story of "VerifyMe" as a sentimental narrative for the campaign rather than creating a fictional persona. The group agreed that this approach would effectively highlight the problem of information silos in domestic security and the necessity of a national database.
Next Steps and Document Access: Seyelnen confirmed they are granting the team edit access to the alignment document, requesting that they provide feedback and corrections directly in the text. The group agreed to continue the review process via the document. While a tentative meeting was proposed for the following week, Esigie Aguele noted they would be out of town but agreed that the rest of the team should proceed with the meeting.

sections.heading: PLUTO VERIFYME.NG - TRUST BEGINS AT HOME
sections.content:
PLUTO VERIFYME.NG - TRUST BEGINS AT HOME
AT HOME
Celebrity-Led Consumer Education Campaign
Moving household security from reactive to proactive through trusted verification

sections.heading: About The Organisation
sections.content:
Pluto (Verifyme.NG)
Pluto operates under Verifyme.NG as a Nigerian technology company specializing in digital identity verification and authentication solutions. The platform serves the Nigerian market with verification technology focused on KYC compliance, identity management, and background screening.
Historically positioned as a B2B background-check service, Pluto now aims to bring its verification infrastructure directly to Nigerian households, enabling families to make informed hiring decisions for domestic workers and artisans.
Digital Identity Verification
Nigerian Market Focus
Established verification technology platform serving Nigerian businesses
Proprietary database infrastructure for employee performance tracking
Unique Pluto Radar feature enabling shared reporting across users
Ready infrastructure for consumer-facing product expansion
Opportunity in Nigeria
Nigerian households consistently hire domestic workers, drivers, nannies, and artisans without adequate background information, creating significant security and trust gaps.
The market opportunity lies in democratizing B2B verification tools for mass consumer use, transforming household hiring from a risk-based gamble into an informed, secure decision.

sections.heading: Context & Core Focus
sections.content:
From Enterprise Background Checks
to Household Peace of Mind
Current Reality - Pluto exists as a B2B verification service known primarily within corporate and HR circles. Consumers hire household staff based on referrals, intuition, or informal networks with no access to verified employment history or performance data.
Strategic Opportunity - Nigerian households represent an untapped mass market desperate for security solutions. By repositioning the same verification technology as a consumer protection tool, Pluto can own the household hiring category while building long-term platform adoption.
Campaign Goal - Shift Pluto from B2B infrastructure to a trusted household name. Use celebrity storytelling and the original VerifyMe origin story to drive awareness, consideration, and conversion among urban millennials and extended demographics up to age 65.

sections.heading: The Problem
sections.content:
Nigerians Hire Blind, Then Hope for the Best
Household hiring happens in an information vacuum, leaving families vulnerable to theft, harm, and broken trust.
Domestic workers and artisans are hired based on word-of-mouth with no verified employment history
Security incidents are reactive - families only verify after something goes wrong
Older demographics rely on children to navigate unfamiliar tech platforms, creating adoption friction
No shared database exists for reporting worker performance or flagging issues across households
Verification is perceived as complex, inconvenient, or only necessary after an incident occurs
The gap is not awareness of risk. The gap is accessible, simple tools that make verification feel urgent before harm happens.

sections.heading: The Objective
sections.content:
Make Household Verification a Non-Negotiable Behaviour
Drive mass adoption of Pluto as the default step before any household hiring decision.
Business Objectives
Transition Pluto from B2B service to mass-market consumer brand
Achieve 120,000 registered consumer users within 12 months
Establish Pluto Radar as the trusted shared database for household hiring
Build sustainable user acquisition through referral loops and platform stickiness
Behaviour Objectives
Normalize verification as a proactive habit, not a post-incident reaction
Shift hiring decisions from trust-based referrals to data-informed choices
Empower older demographics to engage with verification through simplified onboarding
Create peer accountability through shared reporting and transparent worker histories

sections.heading: The Market / Core Audience
sections.content:
Urban Millennials with Household Hiring Responsibility (25-65)
Middle-income Nigerian families hiring domestic workers, drivers, nannies, cooks, and artisans for their homes.
Audience Persona
Adaeze Okonkwo - 38
Lives in Lagos, married with two children under 10
Employs a full-time nanny and cleaner, occasionally hires plumbers and electricians
Relies on referrals from friends but has experienced theft and unreliable workers in the past
Tech-comfortable but values simplicity and speed over feature complexity
Willing to pay for peace of mind and proactive security
Trusts celebrity endorsements from figures she respects
Shares household management decisions with extended family members aged 50-65
Market Size
Estimated 4 million Nigerian households actively hiring domestic workers or artisans, concentrated in Lagos, Abuja, and Port Harcourt
Initial Focus
Lagos urban and suburban middle-income families
Abuja professional households
Extended family decision-makers aged 50-65

sections.heading: The Solution / Creator Strategy
sections.content:
Trust the Story, Then Trust the Platform
Celebrity ambassador Adesua Etomi Wellington will anchor the campaign by telling the original VerifyMe origin story - a narrative rooted in real pain, real risk, and a homegrown Nigerian solution. Her credibility, household relatability, and cross-generational appeal make her the bridge between brand and behaviour change.
Supporting creators will demonstrate the platform through real-life use cases, customer testimonials, and product walkthroughs. The campaign moves audiences from emotional connection to practical adoption, using storytelling to create urgency and creator content to remove friction.
Suggested Creator Profiles
Celebrity Ambassador - Trusted household figure with cross-generational reach
Lifestyle Creators - Family-focused influencers sharing hiring experiences
Tech Explainers - Simplifying platform features for non-tech audiences
Customer Advocates - Real Pluto users sharing testimonials and results
Their Roles
Tell the VerifyMe origin story to build emotional connection and brand trust
Demonstrate the Pluto platform with step-by-step walkthroughs and ease-of-use proof
Share real customer stories of incidents avoided and peace of mind gained
Normalize verification as a standard household behaviour through repeated messaging
Drive referral loops by encouraging users to share their own verification experiences
Address older demographics through simplified, reassuring content formats

sections.heading: Go-To-Market / Campaign
sections.content:
Three-Stage Consumer Adoption Journey
(Months 1-3) - Awareness - The Story - Introduce VerifyMe as the trusted solution for household security by educating Nigerians on the risks of hiring without verification. - Activities - Reach 2.4 million Nigerians with the message that hiring without verification is a gamble they no longer need to take.
Adesua Etomi Wellington launches campaign with VerifyMe origin story across Instagram, Facebook, TikTok
Emotional storytelling content highlighting real household incidents and preventable harm
Paid media amplification targeting urban millennials and household decision-makers
PR seeding around household security trends and verification technology
(Months 4-7) - Consideration - The Product - Use creator stories, customer testimonials, and product demonstrations to encourage platform exploration and understanding. - Activities - Move 600,000 Nigerians from awareness to active platform consideration and account exploration.
Lifestyle creators share real-life use cases of verifying nannies, drivers, and artisans
Tech explainer content walking through Pluto onboarding, Radar feature, and reporting tools
Customer testimonial videos from early adopters sharing peace of mind and positive experiences
Retargeting campaigns to awareness audience with product education and ease-of-use proof
(Months 8-12) - Conversion - The Habit - Convert interested audiences into registered users through targeted campaigns, limited offers, and referral incentives. - Activities - Achieve 120,000 registered users actively using Pluto to verify household hires and contribute to the shared database.
Strong call-to-action campaigns with limited-time onboarding offers and first-verification discounts
Referral program activation encouraging users to invite friends and family
Adesua-led conversion push emphasizing the one-time cost of peace of mind versus lifetime risk
Platform optimization based on user feedback to reduce friction for older demographics
(Ongoing) - Retention - The Community - Build platform stickiness through shared reporting, repeat verification use, and community-driven accountability. - Activities - Create a self-sustaining verification culture where users return to the platform for every new hire and contribute to collective security.
Encourage users to log worker performance and flag issues on Pluto Radar
Seasonal campaigns around holiday hiring peaks and new worker onboarding moments
User-generated content showcasing real stories of verification preventing incidents
Ambassador partnerships with household management influencers for sustained visibility

sections.heading: Risk & Mitigation Analysis
sections.content:
Risk & Mitigation Analysis
Platform perceived as too complex or inconvenient for quick household hiring decisions - Showcase simple, fast user journey through product demos, creator walkthroughs, and clear messaging around speed and ease of use. Optimize onboarding flow based on early user feedback.
Low urgency - consumers only seek verification after an incident occurs rather than proactively - Preventive messaging emphasizes peace of mind and proactive protection. Emotional storytelling from Adesua and real testimonials create urgency before harm happens.
Difficulty converting awareness into paid users due to cost sensitivity or perceived value gap - Use testimonials, limited-time offers, and strong calls-to-action to move users from interest to adoption. Highlight the one-time cost versus lifetime risk positioning.
Older demographics struggle with tech adoption and rely on children to navigate platform - Create simplified onboarding content specifically for non-tech audiences. Use Adesua to model intergenerational use and reassure older users. Offer phone support during pilot phase.
Database growth depends on user contributions - slow Radar adoption limits platform value - Incentivize reporting through referral rewards and community recognition. Make reporting simple and emphasize collective security benefits.
Celebrity ambassador association limits brand independence or creates over-reliance on single voice - Build supporting creator ecosystem early. Transition Adesua from lead storyteller to brand advocate while elevating customer stories and user-generated content.

sections.heading: Budget Assumptions
sections.content:
12-Month Pilot Investment
Estimated Budget
$150,000 - $200,000 USD
Budget Includes
Celebrity ambassador partnership - Adesua Etomi Wellington (storytelling, campaign launch, sustained visibility)
Supporting creator partnerships - lifestyle, tech explainer, and customer advocate content
Paid media - Meta, TikTok, Google, YouTube amplification across awareness, consideration, conversion stages
Content production - origin story video, product demos, testimonials, user walkthroughs
Platform optimization - UX improvements for older demographics and onboarding friction reduction
Referral program activation - incentive structure, tracking, and promotion
Campaign management - strategy, creator coordination, performance tracking, reporting
Contingency - 10% for platform adjustments and market response flexibility
A successful pilot unlocks national expansion, additional creator tiers, and sustained investment in platform-driven community growth.

sections.heading: Talent Suggestions / Team
sections.content:
Recommended Creator Mix
Adesua Etomi Wellington - 8M+ across Instagram, Facebook, Twitter - Trusted household name with cross-generational appeal, credibility in family and lifestyle spaces, and storytelling strength to anchor the VerifyMe origin narrative - Celebrity Ambassador - Campaign anchor, origin story lead, sustained brand voice across all stages
Supporting Lifestyle Creators (TBD based on audience alignment) - 500K-2M per creator - Family-focused influencers who share relatable household hiring experiences and model proactive verification behaviour - Awareness & Consideration - Real-life use cases, product demonstrations, testimonial amplification
Tech Explainer Creators (TBD based on platform simplicity focus) - 200K-1M per creator - Ability to break down Pluto features for non-tech audiences, especially older demographics requiring reassurance and guidance - Consideration - Platform walkthroughs, onboarding tutorials, ease-of-use proof
Customer Advocates (Real Pluto Users) - Organic reach through user-generated content - Authentic testimonials from actual users sharing peace of mind, incidents avoided, and positive verification experiences - Conversion & Retention - Social proof, referral encouragement, community building
Why This Mix Works
Adesua Etomi Wellington provides the emotional anchor and trust layer required to move a mass audience from skepticism to belief. Her household credibility makes verification feel urgent, accessible, and culturally relevant.
Supporting lifestyle creators demonstrate practical adoption and normalize verification as everyday behaviour. They move audiences from belief to consideration by showing real families using the platform in real hiring scenarios.
Tech explainers reduce friction for non-tech users and older demographics, addressing the convenience barrier head-on. Their content transforms platform complexity into simplicity, removing adoption resistance.
Customer advocates provide the social proof that drives conversion. Real users sharing real results create the peer pressure and community accountability that turn individual adoption into collective behaviour change.
Supporting creator selections will be finalized during onboarding to ensure audience alignment, platform strength, and content quality standards.

Content Production & Amplification
