Creator content coordination and quality assurance
Paid media planning, execution, and budget management across Meta, TikTok, Google
Platform optimization support and UX feedback loops
Client Partnership & Platform Integration
Pluto internal stakeholder alignment and briefing
Platform feature prioritization based on campaign learnings
Referral program design and tracking integration
Customer support coordination for pilot phase user inquiries

sections.heading: Closing Statement
sections.content:
Trust Cannot Be Purchased After the Incident
Nigerian households are hiring blind every single day. Pluto has the infrastructure, the technology, and the database to change that behaviour - but infrastructure does not move markets. Stories do. Trust does. Urgency does.
This campaign transforms Pluto from a B2B service into a household necessity by making verification feel urgent before harm happens, simple enough for anyone to use, and socially reinforced through shared accountability. A successful pilot does not just deliver 120,000 users. It creates a verification culture that becomes the new standard for how Nigerians hire, protect their families, and build collective security. That culture is worth far more than the campaign investment.

connect.meeting_purpose:
TASCK would like to talk through your brand and what you are working to achieve, so we can shape the right approach with you. We would like to cover:

1. Your brand / organisation - who you are, what you do, and who you serve.
2. Core Focus Areas - the priorities that matter most to you right now.
3. Campaign Type - the kind of work or campaign you have in mind.
4. Key Audience / Beneficiaries - the people you are trying to reach or serve.
5. Audience Behaviour / Pain Points - what they do today, and what gets in their way.

Duration: October - December 2026

The Opportunity:
House of Jenjie is a premium Nigerian herbal tea brand launching caffeine-free wellness blends that reposition local tea from traditional medicine to world-class lifestyle products. - Lifestyle product not medicinal remedy
- Available at trusted supermarket retailers
- World-class quality meets local heritage

Your Role:
You are House of Jenjie's Wellness Lifestyle Ambassador, the trusted voice that introduces premium Nigerian tea as a daily ritual for health-conscious consumers who shop with intention. You embody the shift from 'what does it cure?' to 'how does it elevate my day?'.
This shows up as authentic integration into your wellness routines, shopping hauls from premium retailers, and conversations that position House of Jenjie as part of a curated lifestyle your audience already aspires to live.

Nigerian herbal tea is no longer medicine - it is premium wellness your lifestyle deserves.
Your content should bring these four pillars to life:
- Premium Repositioning - local ingredients meet world-class standards
- Lifestyle Integration - daily rituals not occasional remedies
- Retail Visibility - supermarket presence builds trust and accessibility
- Health-Conscious Choice - caffeine-free wellness for mindful consumers

2. Lifestyle Integration Content

3. Retail Awareness and Call-to-Action
- Feature supermarket shopping content with House of Jenjie
- Direct audiences to specific retail stockists
- Include digital purchase links for online delivery
4. Community Engagement and Conversion
- Host wellness conversations around premium Nigerian products
- Engage followers on health-conscious lifestyle choices
- Drive awareness that converts to purchase intent

Content is not one-off, it is a series designed to:

- Drive supermarket awareness and product trial

Your creativity is key, but every piece of content should move your audience to act.

- Performance-based commercial incentives tied to sales

  - Documented conversion via tracked links
  - Audience reach and engagement thresholds

pitch_deck.title: House of Jenjie - Creator Campaign Pitch

sections.heading: The Jenjies Lifestyle
sections.content:
The Jenjies Lifestyle
Lifestyle
Creator-Led Premium Tea Repositioning
From herbal remedy to lifestyle essential—building Nigerian wellness heritage

sections.heading: About The Organisation
sections.content:
House of Jenjie
House of Jenjie produces premium caffeine-free herbal tea crafted for the Nigerian wellness consumer. The brand combines indigenous botanical knowledge with world-class product standards, offering a premium alternative to imported wellness teas.
Currently available in select premium supermarkets across Nigeria, House of Jenjie is positioned to compete with established international brands while celebrating Nigerian herbal heritage.
FMCG - Premium Wellness
Caffeine-Free Herbal Tea
Premium herbal tea formulated for health-conscious Nigerian consumers
Caffeine-free positioning for lifestyle wellness rather than medicinal use
Distribution through premium supermarket channels nationwide
Competing in the growing ₦12 billion Nigerian tea and wellness beverage market
Opportunity in Nigeria
Nigeria's middle-to-upper class is rapidly expanding wellness spending, seeking premium products that align with health goals and lifestyle curation. The tea category is dominated by international brands, creating space for a credible local premium player.
The challenge: Nigerian herbal teas are perceived as medicinal agbo, not lifestyle choices. Success requires repositioning the entire category while building brand awareness that drives supermarket offtake.

sections.heading: Context & Core Focus
sections.content:
From Medicine Shelf
to Lifestyle Choice
Current Reality - Nigerian herbal teas sit in the pharmacy aisle, not the pantry. Consumers ask 'what does it cure?' rather than 'when do I enjoy it?' The category is stuck in remedial positioning while international brands own the premium wellness space.
Strategic Opportunity - Affluent Nigerians curate every lifestyle choice—from gyms to skincare to coffee brands. They attend wellness events, follow health influencers, and shop premium supermarkets. They want Nigerian products they can be proud of, but awareness drives purchase intent.
Campaign Goal - Reposition House of Jenjie as a world-class wellness brand that happens to be Nigerian. Build enough consumer awareness and demand to pull product through supermarket shelves, converting social engagement into measurable retail sales within 90 days.

sections.heading: The Problem
sections.content:
Awareness Doesn't Exist Where Purchase Happens
Premium supermarket shoppers don't seek out brands they've never heard of, no matter how good the product.
House of Jenjie has supermarket distribution but limited consumer awareness to drive offtake
Target consumers associate Nigerian herbal tea with medicine, not with daily wellness rituals
The brand cannot rely on founder visibility due to Jennifer's time constraints and strategic preference
International tea brands dominate mindshare in the wellness space—Pukka, Lipton, Twinings own the shelf
Without demand creation, distributors deprioritise the brand and shelf space shrinks
The gap is not product quality or distribution. The gap is consumer awareness that creates pull-through demand at the point of purchase.

sections.heading: The Objective
sections.content:
Drive 5,000-15,000 Sales in 90 Days Through Creator-Led Awareness
Build brand visibility and purchase intent among premium wellness consumers using health and lifestyle influencers as brand surrogates.
Business Objectives
Achieve 5,000 to 15,000 single tea box sales across three months (Oct-Dec 2025)
Strengthen retailer confidence and secure expanded shelf presence in Q1 2026
Establish House of Jenjie as a recognised name in Nigerian premium wellness
Build a repeatable creator-led model that can scale beyond the pilot phase
Behaviour Objectives
Shift perception of Nigerian herbal tea from remedy to lifestyle wellness product
Drive active product search and purchase in premium supermarkets and online platforms
Create habitual tea rituals—morning wellness, afternoon calm, evening wind-down
Generate word-of-mouth recommendations within health-conscious social circles

sections.heading: The Market / Core Audience
sections.content:
Affluent Wellness Curators (35-45)
Middle-to-upper class Nigerians who treat health as a lifestyle category, not a necessity.
Audience Persona
Adanna - 39
Shops at premium supermarkets—Shoprite, Ebeano, The Palms, Spar
Attends wellness events, follows health and lifestyle influencers on Instagram
Actively manages caffeine intake and seeks natural alternatives
Reads product labels and values clean ingredients over price
Participates in fitness communities, yoga classes, or wellness WhatsApp groups
Prefers Nigerian-made products when they match international standards
Shares lifestyle choices on social media and influences peer purchasing decisions
Market Size
Estimated 2.5 million middle-to-upper class Nigerians aged 30-50 in Lagos, Abuja, and Port Harcourt with disposable income for premium wellness products.
Initial Focus
Lagos (Victoria Island, Lekki, Ikoyi) and Abuja (Wuse, Maitama, Asokoro)
Instagram and TikTok users aged 30-45 with wellness and lifestyle interests
Shoppers at premium supermarket chains with existing House of Jenjie distribution

sections.heading: The Solution / Creator Strategy
sections.content:
Position Creators as Wellness Authorities, Not Brand Ambassadors
Rather than using Jennifer as the brand face, we deploy trusted health and lifestyle creators to introduce House of Jenjie as part of their existing wellness routines. The strategy is integration, not interruption—creators share how the tea fits into rituals their audiences already trust.
The campaign uses a single high-authority creator with deep wellness credibility to drive awareness and legitimacy. Ifedayo Agoro becomes the bridge between Nigerian herbal heritage and modern lifestyle wellness, repositioning the category while driving measurable purchase behaviour.
Suggested Creator Profiles
Health and wellness educators with medical or nutritional authority
Lifestyle curators who share daily routines, morning rituals, and self-care habits
Fitness and mindfulness influencers focused on holistic health

Introduce House of Jenjie as part of personal wellness rituals in authentic, unscripted content

Create shoppable moments with clear calls-to-action linking to supermarket and online purchase

sections.heading: Risk & Mitigation Analysis
sections.content:
Risk & Mitigation Analysis
Online interest does not convert to offline supermarket sales - Include direct purchase links to supermarket e-commerce platforms and delivery apps in all creator content. Track digital-to-physical attribution through promo codes and SKU-level sales data.
Single creator dependency creates campaign fragility if content underperforms - Structure content calendar with performance checkpoints at weeks 2, 4, and 8. Build contingency budget for rapid creative pivots or supplementary micro-influencer activation if needed.
Retailer stock-outs during peak demand periods damage campaign momentum - Align campaign launch with confirmed stock levels at priority retailers. Establish direct communication channel with distributors to monitor inventory and trigger restocks before depletion.
Audience perceives campaign as inauthentic brand partnership rather than genuine wellness content - Brief creators to integrate product naturally into existing content formats and wellness routines. Prioritise long-term use documentation over one-off promotional posts. Allow creative freedom within brand guidelines.
Category perception shift takes longer than 90-day campaign window - Set realistic expectations that pilot validates model rather than completing full repositioning. Use campaign learnings to refine messaging and scale creator roster in 2026 expansion phase.
Budget allocation between creator fees and media spend is misbalanced - Cap individual creator investment at ₦10 million while reserving budget for content boosting, retailer collaboration, and performance-based optimisation. Maintain flexibility to shift spend based on early results.

sections.heading: Talent Suggestions / Team
sections.content:
Recommended Creator Mix
Ifedayo Agoro - 500K+ (Instagram/TikTok combined) - Established health and lifestyle authority with deep wellness credibility among target demographic. Known for transparent product reviews, clean-living advocacy, and educational health content that aligns with House of Jenjie's repositioning goals. - Primary brand educator and wellness authority. Responsible for category repositioning content, ingredient education, daily ritual integration, and driving purchase behaviour through authentic product storytelling over 90 days.
Why This Mix Works
Single high-authority creator strategy minimises fragmentation while maximising trust and message consistency. Ifedayo's wellness credibility allows her to reposition the entire herbal tea category, not just promote a product.
Her audience matches the target demographic precisely—affluent, health-conscious Nigerians aged 30-45 who shop premium supermarkets and curate lifestyle choices. High engagement rates suggest strong purchase influence within this segment.
Content format diversity across Instagram Reels, TikTok, and YouTube allows full-funnel activation from awareness to conversion. Long-form educational content builds authority while short-form drives impulse and habitual behaviour.
Capping individual creator investment at ₦10 million reserves budget flexibility for performance optimisation, paid amplification, and potential supplementary activations if early results warrant expansion.

sections.heading: Closing Statement
sections.content:
Build the Brand Nigerians Are Waiting to Buy
House of Jenjie has the product, the distribution, and the positioning to compete with international wellness brands. What it needs is awareness that drives demand at the moment of purchase. This campaign creates that awareness using trusted voices in the exact communities where your customers make lifestyle decisions.
Ninety days. One high-authority creator. A clear path from social proof to supermarket shelf. The goal is not just sales—it is validation that Nigerian herbal tea can own the premium wellness space when introduced with the right strategy. This pilot builds the model. Scale comes next.

about.title: House of Jenjie
paragraphs: House of Jenjie produces premium caffeine-free herbal tea crafted for the Nigerian wellness consumer. The brand combines indigenous botanical knowledge with world-class product standards, offering a premium alternative to imported wellness teas.
Currently available in select premium supermarkets across Nigeria, House of Jenjie is positioned to compete with established international brands while celebrating Nigerian herbal heritage.

callout.title: Opportunity in Nigeria
paragraphs: Nigeria's middle-to-upper class is rapidly expanding wellness spending, seeking premium products that align with health goals and lifestyle curation. The tea category is dominated by international brands, creating space for a credible local premium player.

The challenge: Nigerian herbal teas are perceived as medicinal agbo, not lifestyle choices. Success requires repositioning the entire category while building brand awareness that drives supermarket offtake.

columns.label: Current Reality
columns.body: Nigerian herbal teas sit in the pharmacy aisle, not the pantry. Consumers ask 'what does it cure?' rather than 'when do I enjoy it?' The category is stuck in remedial positioning while international brands own the premium wellness space.

columns.label: Strategic Opportunity
columns.body: Affluent Nigerians curate every lifestyle choice—from gyms to skincare to coffee brands. They attend wellness events, follow health influencers, and shop premium supermarkets. They want Nigerian products they can be proud of, but awareness drives purchase intent.

columns.label: Campaign Goal
columns.body: Reposition House of Jenjie as a world-class wellness brand that happens to be Nigerian. Build enough consumer awareness and demand to pull product through supermarket shelves, converting social engagement into measurable retail sales within 90 days.

problem.title: Awareness Doesn't Exist Where Purchase Happens
problem.lead: Premium supermarket shoppers don't seek out brands they've never heard of, no matter how good the product.
bullets: House of Jenjie has supermarket distribution but limited consumer awareness to drive offtake
Target consumers associate Nigerian herbal tea with medicine, not with daily wellness rituals
The brand cannot rely on founder visibility due to Jennifer's time constraints and strategic preference
International tea brands dominate mindshare in the wellness space—Pukka, Lipton, Twinings own the shelf
Without demand creation, distributors deprioritise the brand and shelf space shrinks
problem.highlight: The gap is not product quality or distribution. The gap is consumer awareness that creates pull-through demand at the point of purchase.

Build a repeatable creator-led model that can scale beyond the pilot phase

sections.heading: Service Agreement
sections.content: This Service Agreement is dated 2026-09-02 and is made between TASCK Creative Company Limited, trading as The TASCK Agency ('TASCK'), and House of Jenjie ('Brand') for the project titled House of Jenjie - Business Call Connect. It is written to be reviewed easily before approval and signature. It explains the project scope, responsibilities, commercial terms, approval process, delivery expectations, cancellation rules, and close-out requirements.

sections.heading: 1. Parties
sections.content:
Party 1: TASCK Creative Company Limited, a registered company situated in Lagos, Nigeria.
Party 2: House of Jenjie.

TASCK and the Brand may be referred to individually as a Party and collectively as the Parties. The Parties agree to work together professionally, respond to project communications within reasonable timelines, and keep all approval decisions clear and documented.

sections.heading: 2. Background and Purpose
sections.content: The Brand has engaged TASCK to support the planning and delivery of House of Jenjie - Business Call Connect. TASCK has the strategy, creator coordination, project management, production support, and reporting capability required to deliver the approved work. The purpose of this Agreement is to record the commercial and operational terms under which TASCK will provide those services.

sections.heading: 3. Scope of Services
sections.content: TASCK will provide services that may include strategy development, creator recommendation and coordination, creative briefing, project planning, production support, content or activation oversight, performance tracking, stakeholder communication, reporting, and project close-out. The exact deliverables, dates, channels, and approval steps will follow the approved Strategy Snapshot, creator brief, deliverables schedule, and any later written amendments approved by both Parties.

sections.heading: 4. Brand Responsibilities
sections.content: The Brand will provide accurate business information, timely approvals, access to required assets, brand guidelines, payment information, stakeholder availability, and feedback needed for TASCK to deliver the project. Delays in approval, funding, asset delivery, or stakeholder response may affect timelines and may require a revised delivery schedule.

sections.heading: 5. Commercial Terms and Payment
sections.content: The total fixed fee or approved working budget for this project is ₦20,000,000. Payment will follow the approved budget and payment schedule. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, the first payment tranche is required before work begins, and any balance is due according to the agreed milestone or final delivery schedule. Work outside the approved scope, including additional creators, extra production days, usage extensions, paid media rights, venue costs, third-party services, rush delivery, or revised deliverables, must be approved in writing before TASCK proceeds.

sections.heading: 6. Project Timeline and Approvals
sections.content: The project timeline will be confirmed through the approved Strategy Snapshot, deliverables schedule, and execution plan. TASCK will submit key materials for review where approval is required. The Brand should provide consolidated feedback so the project can move efficiently. Any change in approval route, decision maker, launch date, budget, or legal requirement must be communicated to TASCK as soon as it is known.

sections.heading: 7. Performance, Reporting, and Acceptance
sections.content: TASCK will coordinate delivery and provide a final report using the information available from the approved deliverables, creator outputs, campaign performance, and project records. The Brand will review the final report and provide feedback or acceptance within a reasonable period. Once accepted, the project may be closed in TASCK.

sections.heading: 8. Intellectual Property and Usage
sections.content: Ownership and usage rights for project materials will follow the approved brief, creator contracts, paid usage terms, and any written rights schedule. TASCK does not grant rights beyond those actually secured from creators, production partners, or third parties. The Brand must not extend usage, paid media, territory, duration, exclusivity, or adaptation beyond the approved rights without written confirmation.

sections.heading: 9. Confidentiality
sections.content: Each Party will keep confidential information private, including campaign plans, commercial terms, project documents, unpublished creative, contact information, account access, strategy materials, creator negotiations, and performance data. Confidential information may only be shared with people who need it to perform the project.

sections.heading: 10. Cancellation, Delay, and Scope Changes
sections.content: If the Brand cancels, pauses, or materially changes the project after work has begun, TASCK will document the effect on schedule, cost, deliverables, third-party commitments, and creator obligations. The Brand remains responsible for approved work already completed, committed costs, cancellation charges, and reasonable time already spent. TASCK will not proceed with new or expanded work until the Parties approve the change in writing.

sections.heading: 11. Liability and Professional Conduct
sections.content: Each Party is responsible for its own negligence, misconduct, breach of confidentiality, and failure to meet documented obligations. Neither Party is responsible for delay or failure caused by events beyond reasonable control, including platform outages, government restrictions, force majeure events, third-party failure, or delayed approvals outside that Party's control.

sections.heading: 12. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution
sections.content: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. The Parties will first attempt to resolve any dispute through good-faith discussion. If unresolved, the dispute may be referred to arbitration in accordance with applicable Nigerian arbitration law.

pitch_deck.title: House of Jenjie - Creator Campaign Pitch

sections.heading: The Jenjies Lifestyle
sections.content:
The Jenjies Lifestyle
Lifestyle
Creator-Led Premium Tea Repositioning
From herbal remedy to lifestyle essential—building Nigerian wellness heritage

sections.heading: About The Organisation
sections.content:
House of Jenjie
House of Jenjie produces premium caffeine-free herbal tea crafted for the Nigerian wellness consumer. The brand combines indigenous botanical knowledge with world-class product standards, offering a premium alternative to imported wellness teas.
Currently available in select premium supermarkets across Nigeria, House of Jenjie is positioned to compete with established international brands while celebrating Nigerian herbal heritage.
FMCG - Premium Wellness
Caffeine-Free Herbal Tea
Premium herbal tea formulated for health-conscious Nigerian consumers
Caffeine-free positioning for lifestyle wellness rather than medicinal use
Distribution through premium supermarket channels nationwide
Competing in the growing ₦12 billion Nigerian tea and wellness beverage market
Opportunity in Nigeria
Nigeria's middle-to-upper class is rapidly expanding wellness spending, seeking premium products that align with health goals and lifestyle curation. The tea category is dominated by international brands, creating space for a credible local premium player.
The challenge: Nigerian herbal teas are perceived as medicinal agbo, not lifestyle choices. Success requires repositioning the entire category while building brand awareness that drives supermarket offtake.

sections.heading: Context & Core Focus
sections.content:
From Medicine Shelf
to Lifestyle Choice
Current Reality - Nigerian herbal teas sit in the pharmacy aisle, not the pantry. Consumers ask 'what does it cure?' rather than 'when do I enjoy it?' The category is stuck in remedial positioning while international brands own the premium wellness space.
Strategic Opportunity - Affluent Nigerians curate every lifestyle choice—from gyms to skincare to coffee brands. They attend wellness events, follow health influencers, and shop premium supermarkets. They want Nigerian products they can be proud of, but awareness drives purchase intent.
Campaign Goal - Reposition House of Jenjie as a world-class wellness brand that happens to be Nigerian. Build enough consumer awareness and demand to pull product through supermarket shelves, converting social engagement into measurable retail sales within 90 days.

sections.heading: The Problem
sections.content:
Awareness Doesn't Exist Where Purchase Happens
Premium supermarket shoppers don't seek out brands they've never heard of, no matter how good the product.
House of Jenjie has supermarket distribution but limited consumer awareness to drive offtake
Target consumers associate Nigerian herbal tea with medicine, not with daily wellness rituals
The brand cannot rely on founder visibility due to Jennifer's time constraints and strategic preference
International tea brands dominate mindshare in the wellness space—Pukka, Lipton, Twinings own the shelf
Without demand creation, distributors deprioritise the brand and shelf space shrinks
The gap is not product quality or distribution. The gap is consumer awareness that creates pull-through demand at the point of purchase.

sections.heading: The Objective
sections.content:
Drive 5,000-15,000 Sales in 90 Days Through Creator-Led Awareness
Build brand visibility and purchase intent among premium wellness consumers using health and lifestyle influencers as brand surrogates.
Business Objectives
Achieve 5,000 to 15,000 single tea box sales across three months (Oct-Dec 2025)
Strengthen retailer confidence and secure expanded shelf presence in Q1 2026
Establish House of Jenjie as a recognised name in Nigerian premium wellness
Build a repeatable creator-led model that can scale beyond the pilot phase
Behaviour Objectives
Shift perception of Nigerian herbal tea from remedy to lifestyle wellness product
Drive active product search and purchase in premium supermarkets and online platforms
Create habitual tea rituals—morning wellness, afternoon calm, evening wind-down
Generate word-of-mouth recommendations within health-conscious social circles

sections.heading: The Market / Core Audience
sections.content:
Affluent Wellness Curators (35-45)
Middle-to-upper class Nigerians who treat health as a lifestyle category, not a necessity.
Audience Persona
Adanna - 39
Shops at premium supermarkets—Shoprite, Ebeano, The Palms, Spar
Attends wellness events, follows health and lifestyle influencers on Instagram
Actively manages caffeine intake and seeks natural alternatives
Reads product labels and values clean ingredients over price
Participates in fitness communities, yoga classes, or wellness WhatsApp groups
Prefers Nigerian-made products when they match international standards
Shares lifestyle choices on social media and influences peer purchasing decisions
Market Size
Estimated 2.5 million middle-to-upper class Nigerians aged 30-50 in Lagos, Abuja, and Port Harcourt with disposable income for premium wellness products.
Initial Focus
Lagos (Victoria Island, Lekki, Ikoyi) and Abuja (Wuse, Maitama, Asokoro)
Instagram and TikTok users aged 30-45 with wellness and lifestyle interests
Shoppers at premium supermarket chains with existing House of Jenjie distribution

sections.heading: The Solution / Creator Strategy
sections.content:
Position Creators as Wellness Authorities, Not Brand Ambassadors
Rather than using Jennifer as the brand face, we deploy trusted health and lifestyle creators to introduce House of Jenjie as part of their existing wellness routines. The strategy is integration, not interruption—creators share how the tea fits into rituals their audiences already trust.
The campaign uses a single high-authority creator with deep wellness credibility to drive awareness and legitimacy. Ifedayo Agoro becomes the bridge between Nigerian herbal heritage and modern lifestyle wellness, repositioning the category while driving measurable purchase behaviour.
Suggested Creator Profiles
Health and wellness educators with medical or nutritional authority
Lifestyle curators who share daily routines, morning rituals, and self-care habits
Fitness and mindfulness influencers focused on holistic health
Clean-living advocates who review products and ingredients transparently
Their Roles
Introduce House of Jenjie as part of personal wellness rituals in authentic, unscripted content
Educate audiences on caffeine-free benefits and indigenous botanical ingredients
Create shoppable moments with clear calls-to-action linking to supermarket and online purchase
Host wellness challenges or tea rituals that encourage trial and repeat behaviour
Document product experiences over time to build trust and normalise daily use
Drive offline purchase through online influence—social proof that converts at the shelf

sections.heading: Go-To-Market / Campaign
sections.content:
Three-Month Behaviour Change Journey
(Month 1: October 2025) - Awareness & Education - Introduce the brand and reposition the category from remedy to ritual. - Activities - Reach 5 million users and shift perception of Nigerian herbal tea to lifestyle product.
Creator-led content series on caffeine-free wellness and Nigerian herbal heritage
Instagram Reels and TikTok videos showing morning tea rituals and ingredient transparency
Educational carousel posts on health benefits without medicinal framing
Stories documenting first impressions, taste tests, and daily integration
(Month 2: November 2025) - Consideration & Trial - Drive purchase intent and make buying easy through digital and physical retail links. - Activities - Convert awareness into 3,000-5,000 first-time purchases across digital and offline channels.
Shoppable content with direct links to supermarket online platforms and delivery apps
Wellness challenges encouraging followers to try 7-day or 14-day tea rituals
User-generated content campaigns asking audiences to share their tea moments
Retailer collaboration content showing in-store product placement and availability
(Month 3: December 2025) - Habit Formation & Advocacy - Turn trial into repeat behaviour and create word-of-mouth momentum. - Activities - Drive repeat purchases to reach 10,000-15,000 total sales and establish habitual use.
Long-form testimonial content showing sustained use and lifestyle integration
Holiday gifting content positioning House of Jenjie as a premium wellness gift
Community engagement through wellness events or virtual tea tasting sessions
Audience testimonials and reviews shared by creators to validate repeat purchase
(Post-Campaign: January 2026) - Evaluation & Scale - Assess performance, refine approach, and prepare for expanded creator roster. - Activities - Validate the creator-led model and build the case for scaling investment and distribution.
Sales data analysis by channel, region, and creator-driven traffic sources
Retailer feedback sessions to understand shelf movement and reorder patterns
Audience sentiment analysis and content performance review
Strategic planning for Q1 2026 expansion based on pilot learnings

sections.heading: Go-To-Market / Campaign
sections.content:
The Campaign Funnel
Awareness - 5 millionreach across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube
Engagement - 500,000 meaningful interactions—saves, shares, comments, profile visits
Consideration - 50,000 link clicks to purchase platforms and retailer pages
Conversion - 5,000-15,000 purchases across 90 days
Advocacy - 1,000+ user-generated posts and testimonials driving word-of-mouth
Primary Platforms
Instagram (Reels, Stories, Carousels)
TikTok (short-form lifestyle and wellness content)
Secondary Platforms
YouTube (long-form wellness education and product deep-dives)
WhatsApp (community shares and peer recommendations)
Supermarket e-commerce platforms (Shoprite, Spar, Jumia Food)
Wellness event activations and community pop-ups

sections.heading: Campaign Projections
sections.content:
Success Metrics (90 Days)
Community Growth
5 million reach across creator audiences
500,000 engaged users (saves, shares, comments, profile visits)
50,000 clicks to purchase links and retailer platforms
Content
40-60 pieces of creator-led content across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube
1,000+ user-generated content posts using branded hashtags or tea rituals
10+ retailer collaboration posts showing in-store availability
Commercial
5,000-15,000 single tea box sales across three months
20-30% repeat purchase rate among first-time buyers
Expanded shelf presence in 3-5 additional premium supermarket locations
Behaviour
Shift in consumer language from 'what does it cure?' to 'when do I drink it?'
Increased retailer confidence leading to reorders and feature placements
Established tea rituals among early adopters driving habitual consumption
Validated creator-led model ready for scale in 2026

sections.heading: Risk & Mitigation Analysis
sections.content:
Risk & Mitigation Analysis
Online interest does not convert to offline supermarket sales - Include direct purchase links to supermarket e-commerce platforms and delivery apps in all creator content. Track digital-to-physical attribution through promo codes and SKU-level sales data.
Single creator dependency creates campaign fragility if content underperforms - Structure content calendar with performance checkpoints at weeks 2, 4, and 8. Build contingency budget for rapid creative pivots or supplementary micro-influencer activation if needed.
Retailer stock-outs during peak demand periods damage campaign momentum - Align campaign launch with confirmed stock levels at priority retailers. Establish direct communication channel with distributors to monitor inventory and trigger restocks before depletion.
Audience perceives campaign as inauthentic brand partnership rather than genuine wellness content - Brief creators to integrate product naturally into existing content formats and wellness routines. Prioritise long-term use documentation over one-off promotional posts. Allow creative freedom within brand guidelines.
Category perception shift takes longer than 90-day campaign window - Set realistic expectations that pilot validates model rather than completing full repositioning. Use campaign learnings to refine messaging and scale creator roster in 2026 expansion phase.
Budget allocation between creator fees and media spend is misbalanced - Cap individual creator investment at ₦10 million while reserving budget for content boosting, retailer collaboration, and performance-based optimisation. Maintain flexibility to shift spend based on early results.

sections.heading: Budget Assumptions
sections.content:
90-Day Pilot Investment
Estimated Budget
₦20,000,000 total campaign investment
Budget Includes
Creator partnership fees capped at ₦10,000,000 per creator for 90-day activation
Content production support including product styling, photography, and videography
Paid media budget for boosting high-performing organic content on Instagram and TikTok
Retailer collaboration costs including in-store activations and promotional materials
E-commerce platform integration and shoppable link infrastructure
Campaign management, strategy, and performance tracking by TASCK team
Contingency reserve for rapid creative pivots or supplementary influencer activation
Post-campaign analysis, reporting, and strategic recommendations for 2026 scale
A successful pilot unlocks expanded creator roster, broader geographic reach, and increased retailer investment for Q1 2026 scaling phase.

sections.heading: Talent Suggestions / Team
sections.content:
Recommended Creator Mix
Ifedayo Agoro - 500K+ (Instagram/TikTok combined) - Established health and lifestyle authority with deep wellness credibility among target demographic. Known for transparent product reviews, clean-living advocacy, and educational health content that aligns with House of Jenjie's repositioning goals. - Primary brand educator and wellness authority. Responsible for category repositioning content, ingredient education, daily ritual integration, and driving purchase behaviour through authentic product storytelling over 90 days.
Why This Mix Works
Single high-authority creator strategy minimises fragmentation while maximising trust and message consistency. Ifedayo's wellness credibility allows her to reposition the entire herbal tea category, not just promote a product.
Her audience matches the target demographic precisely—affluent, health-conscious Nigerians aged 30-45 who shop premium supermarkets and curate lifestyle choices. High engagement rates suggest strong purchase influence within this segment.
Content format diversity across Instagram Reels, TikTok, and YouTube allows full-funnel activation from awareness to conversion. Long-form educational content builds authority while short-form drives impulse and habitual behaviour.
Capping individual creator investment at ₦10 million reserves budget flexibility for performance optimisation, paid amplification, and potential supplementary activations if early results warrant expansion.
Audience size estimates based on current platform data. Final reach and engagement projections will be validated during creator contracting and briefing phase.

sections.heading: Delivery Team
sections.content:
Delivery Team
Strategy & Campaign Management
Campaign strategy development and creator briefing aligned to repositioning goals
Content calendar management and performance tracking across 90-day activation
Retailer liaison and e-commerce platform integration coordination
Weekly reporting and real-time optimisation based on engagement and sales data
Creative & Content Production
Creator content support including product styling, photography direction, and videography
Brand guideline development ensuring visual and messaging consistency
User-generated content curation and community management
Paid media creative adaptation and platform-specific optimisation
Media & Performance
Paid social media strategy and budget allocation across Instagram and TikTok
Shoppable content setup and purchase link infrastructure management
Attribution tracking connecting social engagement to supermarket and online sales
Post-campaign analysis including sales data, retailer feedback, and ROI modelling

sections.heading: Closing Statement
sections.content:
Build the Brand Nigerians Are Waiting to Buy
House of Jenjie has the product, the distribution, and the positioning to compete with international wellness brands. What it needs is awareness that drives demand at the moment of purchase. This campaign creates that awareness using trusted voices in the exact communities where your customers make lifestyle decisions.
Ninety days. One high-authority creator. A clear path from social proof to supermarket shelf. The goal is not just sales—it is validation that Nigerian herbal tea can own the premium wellness space when introduced with the right strategy. This pilot builds the model. Scale comes next.

budget.footnote: A successful pilot unlocks expanded creator roster, broader geographic reach, and increased retailer investment for Q1 2026 scaling phase.

creator_mix.title: Recommended Creator Mix

rows.creator: Ifedayo Agoro
rows.why: Established health and lifestyle authority with deep wellness credibility among target demographic. Known for transparent product reviews, clean-living advocacy, and educational health content that aligns with House of Jenjie's repositioning goals.
rows.role: Primary brand educator and wellness authority. Responsible for category repositioning content, ingredient education, daily ritual integration, and driving purchase behaviour through authentic product storytelling over 90 days.

why_works: Single high-authority creator strategy minimises fragmentation while maximising trust and message consistency. Ifedayo's wellness credibility allows her to reposition the entire herbal tea category, not just promote a product.

Her audience matches the target demographic precisely—affluent, health-conscious Nigerians aged 30-45 who shop premium supermarkets and curate lifestyle choices. High engagement rates suggest strong purchase influence within this segment.

Content format diversity across Instagram Reels, TikTok, and YouTube allows full-funnel activation from awareness to conversion. Long-form educational content builds authority while short-form drives impulse and habitual behaviour.

Capping individual creator investment at ₦10 million reserves budget flexibility for performance optimisation, paid amplification, and potential supplementary activations if early results warrant expansion.
creator_mix.footnote: Audience size estimates based on current platform data. Final reach and engagement projections will be validated during creator contracting and briefing phase.

closing.title: Build the Brand Nigerians Are Waiting to Buy
paragraphs: House of Jenjie has the product, the distribution, and the positioning to compete with international wellness brands. What it needs is awareness that drives demand at the moment of purchase. This campaign creates that awareness using trusted voices in the exact communities where your customers make lifestyle decisions.

Ninety days. One high-authority creator. A clear path from social proof to supermarket shelf. The goal is not just sales—it is validation that Nigerian herbal tea can own the premium wellness space when introduced with the right strategy. This pilot builds the model. Scale comes next.

opportunities.title: House of Jenjie Brand Launch & Awareness Campaign
opportunities.summary: Jennifer needs strategic marketing support to launch House of Jenjie caffeine-free herbal tea as a premium Nigerian wellness brand. The goal is to reposition Nigerian tea from 'medicine/agbo' to a world-class lifestyle product that sits alongside Pukka and Lipton, while driving consumer demand that pulls product through supermarket distribution channels. Jennifer wants to avoid being the face of the brand initially due to time constraints, seeking alternative approaches using health/wellness influencers instead.
opportunities.focus: Brand positioning and consumer awareness campaign to drive supermarket sell-through
opportunities.campaign_type: Product launch and brand awareness campaign
opportunities.audience: Middle-aged (around 40), middle-to-upper class consumers who are health-conscious, can afford premium products, shop for lifestyle rather than necessity, attend community events, and are mindful about processed foods and artificial ingredients. May or may not have health issues but watch caffeine levels.
opportunities.audience_behaviour: Currently associate Nigerian tea with medicine ('what does it cure?') rather than premium wellness. Shop at premium supermarkets but need to be aware of brands before seeking them out. Curate lifestyle choices and participate in health/wellness social circles.
opportunities.goals: Sell 5,000-15,000 boxes over 12 months across 3 supermarkets in Jos, 5+ outlets in Lagos, and 3 outlets in Abuja. Drive fast-moving inventory at supermarket level to ensure repeat wholesale orders. Position as premium brand available in select spaces (airlines, upscale hotels, cafes) while maintaining scarcity for premium positioning.
opportunities.success_looks_like: Consumer demand drives supermarket reorders within days/weeks rather than monthly. Brand becomes a household name that people specifically ask for at retail. Product achieves premium shelf placement alongside international brands. Fast inventory turnover with no dead stock.
opportunities.timeline: Next 12 months for 5,000 box target; regulatory approval imminent which will unlock supermarket distribution
opportunities.evidence: 'So somewhere between solving that problem that makes me not the focal point, but still communicating the authenticity of how I want the brand to resonate locally and globally... strategic thinking around how to do this marketing well is my current challenge.' Jennifer also stated: 'A lot of the distribution can happen offline... but a lot of the drivers for I want that T, where can I get it, is A one-on-one sort of interaction. That is what I think is level one in the marketing.'
